preserved_objections.basis: The comb-shaped interdigital electrodes approach does not address the fundamental physics of shock-induced contact between comb fingers; the proposed mechanism merely rearranges the electrode geometry without changing the proximity of moving parts during shock events.

The candidate fails to specify critical boundary conditions such as shock duration, frequency spectrum, and environmental constraints that would determine whether the redesigned structure can actually prevent stiction under realistic operating conditions.

The provided evidence bundle consists only of general papers on MEMS accelerometer design and does not include any specific experimental data or theoretical analysis demonstrating that comb-shaped interdigital electrodes reduce stiction in shock scenarios.

The candidate does not address the manufacturing challenges of implementing asymmetric comb structures in MEMS processes, which would require specialized fabrication techniques not compatible with standard CMOS foundries.

The testable prediction focuses only on zero-g offset measurement without specifying acceptable thresholds or defining success criteria, making it impossible to determine if the intervention actually solves the stiction problem.
